sections.h2: What should a Wentzville, MO seller expect?
sections.html:
Wentzville sits in western St. Charles County, and it grew faster by percentage than any other Missouri city between 2000 and 2020, according to Wikipedia. Most homes here are owner-occupied. The city asks for no occupancy inspection on a sale, though the rules change if the buyer plans to rent the house out.

The Census Bureau counted 44,372 people in 2020 and estimates 49,495 for July 1, 2025. The 2010 count was only 29,070, so the population rose about 53 percent in one decade.

sections.h2: What built Wentzville, and who employs its residents?
sections.html:
Wentzville was laid out in 1855 and named for Erasmus Livingston Wentz, a chief engineer of the Northern Missouri Railroad. The post office dates to 1859, and the old Wentzville Tobacco Company Factory has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1990.

General Motors leads local employment through its Wentzville Assembly plant, which makes full-size vans and small trucks. Wikipedia also notes that a federal contractor's processing center employed about 1,500 people here at its peak and closed in 2018, eliminating 850 jobs.

Wentzville spans about 20 square miles. A mayor, six aldermen from three wards and a city administrator run it. Rotary Park hosts the St. Charles County Fair and the St. Louis Renaissance Festival. The Wentzville R-IV School District covers Wentzville, Lake St. Louis, Foristell, Dardenne Prairie and part of O'Fallon, with four public high schools: Holt, Timberland, North Point and Liberty.

sections.h2: How do Wentzville households and home values compare?
sections.html:
Owners live in most Wentzville homes, and households run larger than in University City.

Children under 18 are 29.7 percent of residents, and the average household has 2.86 people. The mean commute of 27.8 minutes is longer than in University City, so a buyer will weigh the drive to St. Louis jobs.

sections.h2: What local details come up when buyers look at Wentzville?
sections.html:
Buyers often ask about schools, nearby colleges and community landmarks, and Wentzville has a few to mention in a listing. Lindenwood University runs a satellite campus in the former Southern Air Restaurant building, which was last owned by Chuck Berry. Degrees are also offered by Midwest University and Urshan University, and the city has a branch of the St. Charles City-County Library serves residents.

The city is home to the first Vietnam Veterans Memorial in the United States. It began in 1967 as a tree of lights to raise money for gifts to servicemen, and by 1984 it had become a carved eagle atop a granite pillar. It is a regular stop on the national Run for the Wall trip. Private schools include St. Patrick School and Immanuel Lutheran School, both covering preschool through eighth grade.

These items do not set a price by themselves, yet a seller who can name the school district, the nearest library and the drive to St. Louis gives buyers and investors a clearer picture of the address.

sections.h2: Does Wentzville require an inspection when I sell my house?
sections.html:
No. The City of Wentzville says no occupancy inspection is required when selling a house. An inspection comes into play only when the house will be leased, and it must pass before a tenant moves in.

  • The residential occupancy inspection costs $50 and stays valid for 90 days.
  • Request it on the city's SmartGov permit portal; once the fee is paid, scheduling normally takes one to two business days.
  • The city requires a new inspection each time the resident changes at a property.
  • A new-construction buyer does not need one, because the builder obtains occupancy with the construction permit.

New service at the address also matters to a buyer: opening a water, trash and sewer account requires a $150 deposit, which the city holds until two years of good payment history and then credits to the account. The Building Division answers questions at (636) 327-5101, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: Which sale routes are open to a Wentzville owner?
sections.html:
Owners usually pick between an agent listing, a sale by owner and a sale to an investor. Because the city asks nothing of a seller for an owner-occupied sale, the difference between them comes down to time, cost and condition.

  • Agent listing. Ask for the commission rate in writing, plus an estimate of repair and staging costs.
  • Sale by owner. You set the price and run showings, and a title company still handles the closing.
  • Investor offer. An investor may take the house in its current condition. One who plans to rent it must pass the $50 occupancy inspection before a tenant moves in.

Tally what you owe first. Any mortgage, home equity line or unpaid property tax is paid from the sale proceeds, so request a payoff statement before comparing offers.

sections.h2: Who collects Wentzville property tax, and how can I pay?
sections.html:
St. Charles County bills property tax for Wentzville. The Collector of Revenue's office is at 201 N. Second Street, Suite 134, in St. Charles, and its phone is 636-949-7470. Partial payments start at $20, but a partial payment will not keep a property out of the tax certificate sale.

  • Online or phone payments by e-check carry a $1.50 fee, and cards cost about 2.5 percent.
  • Mailed payments count on the USPS postmark date. A payment mailed on December 31 may not be postmarked until the next business day.
  • Bank bill-pay services should start at least five working days before December 31, because the county counts the day it receives the money.

To dispute a value, begin with an informal hearing at the Assessor's Office. Hearings run from late April to early June, and outside a reassessment year the number is 636-949-7428. Next comes the Board of Equalization, whose 2026 form was due by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July. That date is past. The last level is the Missouri State Tax Commission, with a filing date of September 30 or 30 days after the Board decision, whichever falls later. Property bought after the second Monday in June gets until December 31. Full instructions are printed on the assessment notice you receive.

sections.h2: Where should a fast Wentzville sale start?
sections.html:
Begin with the figures a buyer will request: your loan payoff, the newest county tax bill, any HOA dues and a list of recent repairs. Then decide how much cleaning and fixing you will pay for before showing it.

To avoid a long listing period, collect written investor offers and set each against a realistic list price minus agent fees, repairs and carrying costs. Read who pays closing costs and what happens if the buyer withdraws. If the house will be rented after the sale, remind the buyer about the city's $50 occupancy inspection and the 90-day validity window so the move-in date is not delayed.

faqs.q: Does Wentzville inspect a house before it is sold?
faqs.a: No. Wentzville states that no occupancy inspection is required by the city when a house is sold. An inspection applies only when the house will be leased or rented to a new tenant.

faqs.q: How much is the Wentzville occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: It costs $50 and is valid for 90 days. It is requested through the SmartGov permit portal and is usually scheduled one to two business days after payment.

faqs.q: Which county bills Wentzville property tax?
faqs.a: St. Charles County does. The Collector of Revenue is at 201 N. Second Street, Suite 134, in St. Charles, and can be reached at 636-949-7470.

faqs.q: Can I still file a 2026 assessment appeal in Wentzville?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Equalization form was due by 5 p.m. on the second Monday of July 2026. A later State Tax Commission appeal needs a prior Board filing unless the property was newly purchased.
About 49,495 people live there by the July 2025 Census estimate, up from 44,372 in 2020, across roughly 20 square miles in western St. Charles County.
